knowledge.display_text: Inflammaging is persistent low-grade age-related inflammation involving IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, IL-13, CRP, IFN-α/β and TNF; it occurs in many older adults and is implicated in multiple age-related diseases, functional decline and mortality.

statements.modality: implicated, not established as a sufficient cause

attributes.name: mediators
attributes.value: IL-1; IL-6; IL-8; IL-13; CRP; IFN-α/β; TNF

attributes.name: associated_conditions
attributes.value: cardiovascular disease; cancer; chronic kidney disease; dementia; depression; sarcopenia; frailty

attributes.name: occurrence
attributes.value: majority of older adults, even without disease or risk factors

knowledge.display_text: Evidence connecting diet and inflammation in older adults is scarce and inconsistent; adequate n-3 PUFA intake appears protective, and cited Italian/Scottish Mediterranean-diet studies followed participants for three/six years. Relations of individual food groups in MCI remain unclear.

Aging alters sleep architecture and increases insomnia, apnea and circadian/quality disturbances; cited studies disagree about sleep–inflammation associations, including a U-shaped objective-sleep relation in cognitively nonimpaired adults.

statements.modality: heterogeneous cited associations, including null findings

knowledge.display_text: Earlier work links leisure exercise to lower circulating inflammatory markers; a 12-week pilot in 30 CNI and 30 MCI participants and a review of MCI/dementia interventions reported reductions, but simple brisk-walking questions were not systematically studied.

MCI involves early memory/other cognitive deficits with independence in most daily activities; cited prevalence is 15–20% after age 60 and annual progression to dementia 8–15%, motivating modifiable risk-factor research.

Test cross-sectional relations of diet, objective/subjective sleep and mild physical activity with plasma TNF-α and IL-6, including whether MCI modifies the associations. The authors hypothesize independent lifestyle relations.

conditions: Cross-sectional Cretan Aging Cohort phase II; complete-data sample of 117 older adults (54 CNI, 63 MCI)

knowledge.display_text: The Cretan Aging Cohort was conducted in urban/rural Heraklion from March 2013 to June 2015 in two phases, with approval 13541 (20 November 2010) and informed consent.
Screen consenting adults over 60 in primary care with trained-nurse interviews and Greek MMSE; use 23/24 because education is often ≤6 years, defining risk as <24 and nonrisk as ≥24.
Phase I retained 3140 participants: 57% women, age 73.7±7.8 years (60–100), education 5.8±3.3 years (0–18), mostly rural.

Invite the 636 people with MMSE <24 for phase II; 344 consented and were comparable on age, sex and BMI. Use extensive clinical/neuropsychological assessment and consensus by ≥2 clinicians under modified Petersen/IWG-1 criteria, excluding deficits explained by significant mood/anxiety disorder.
Operational MCI requires age/education-adjusted z<−1.5 on at least two tests in a memory, language or attention/executive domain, with intact Lawton–Brody instrumental daily activities.

conditions: Cretan phase II modified Petersen/IWG-1 classification

knowledge.display_text: The nonimpaired sampling pool is reported as 2504 people with MMSE >24; 181 stratified controls were invited and 161 consented. Of 505 assessed, 231 had MCI, 128 dementia and 146 CNI.
Select the 117 phase-II participants with complete sleep, diet, activity and plasma-marker data: 54 CNI and 63 MCI. Severe terminal illness or movement impairment was not included.

knowledge.display_text: Study strengths include simultaneous lifestyle assessment, Cretan diet context and practical primary-care questions plus actigraphy, with significant/borderline group findings as interpreted by the authors.

Three-day actigraphy is shorter than the suggested 1–2 weeks; sleep/apnea/activity self-report and unmodeled medication/comorbidity limit inference, and the cross-sectional design cannot establish causality.
